79175.subject: Crypto Didn't Get CLARITY, But it Can Still Get Clarity
79175.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

These are the biggest stories in DeFi and crypto:

* **[The Senate](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/senate-blocks-clarity-act-49-50-with-no-democratic-votes-to-proceed)**[ blocked the CLARITY Act 49-50 with no Democratic votes](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/senate-blocks-clarity-act-49-50-with-no-democratic-votes-to-proceed)

* **[CoinEx](https://thedefiant.io/news/cefi/coinex-to-close-exchange-on-ninth-anniversary)**[ is closing after nine years, with withdrawals ending Dec. 22](https://thedefiant.io/news/cefi/coinex-to-close-exchange-on-ninth-anniversary)

* **[0x](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/0x-says-uniswap-v4-hooks-were-a-mistake-hayden-adams-says-skill-issue)**[ says 54% of Uniswap v4 hooks are malicious; Hayden Adams says skill issue](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/0x-says-uniswap-v4-hooks-were-a-mistake-hayden-adams-says-skill-issue)

* **[An MEV bot](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/mev-bot-front-runs-7-8-million-rseth-exploit-on-ethereum)**[ front-ran a $7.8 million rsETH exploit and kept the proceeds](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/mev-bot-front-runs-7-8-million-rseth-exploit-on-ethereum)

* **[Bitcoin](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-falls-below-76000-clarity-act-odds-senate-vote-sep-15-2026)**[ fell below $76,000 while options traders kept volatility cheap](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-falls-below-76000-clarity-act-odds-senate-vote-sep-15-2026)

* **[Oasis Vault](https://www.oasisvault.io/cryptopunk?utm_source=the_defiant&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=oasis_cryptopunk)**[ is giving away CryptoPunk 909 (Partner)](https://www.oasisvault.io/cryptopunk?utm_source=the_defiant&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=oasis_cryptopunk)

Four hours before the Senate blocked the CLARITY Act, Anchorage Digital's head of policy explained what the industry would do without it.

"Clarity would be really nice to have. It's the big, beautiful present with a bow on top of it," Kevin Wysocki said on The Defiant's livestream Tuesday morning. "But there's a lot of stocking stuffers that are out there too."

The OCC's chief counsel said roughly five years ago that custody of digital assets is effectively the same as traditional asset custody. No law was needed. The five stablecoins Anchorage issues today are issued under that guidance, not under the GENIUS Act, which does not take effect until January. Charter applications are the federal pathway that exists right now, and Wysocki expects more of them, plus more broker-dealer registrations under structures already on the books.

Summer Mersinger, who held a CFTC seat until May 2025 and now runs the Blockchain Association, made the same argument from the legislative side. CLARITY is not the first crypto market structure bill. FIT21 passed the House in May 2024 and died in the Senate. "It's not like this is just going to go away if this vote isn't successful," she said.

79169.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9f199753-ca31-4e3d-9435-5e12896ecff5/BD_NL_Banner_Heading.png?t=1781793903)

Caption: 

“Free scientific inquiry? The first adjective is redundant.”
_— Ayn Rand, __Atlas Shrugged_



----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/496f7a8d-9cbe-4e70-85d9-00ffa300b39e/Screenshot_2026-09-15_at_17.45.32.png?t=1789508773)
Caption: 

# AI without the data center

Blockchains, often accused of being a solution in search of a problem, may have found a big problem to solve: the centralization of AI.

As problems go, it’s been a theoretical one so far. Consumers of AI are currently overrun with free chatbots and open-source models to choose from.

But as the topic of AI safety has now burst into the mainstream, it seems increasingly likely that the big labs that provide us with these chatbots and models will soon be regulated — perhaps in a way that leaves only a handful of government-approved providers able to build any new ones.

That dystopian prospect has inspired a call to action among techno-libertarians and AI accelerationists: “The only possible resistance is to build decentralized, permissionless, and sovereign AI,” the pseudonymous Beff Jezos [said](https://x.com/beffjezos/status/2098861431705972990) on X.

Replace “AI” with “money” and it’s exactly what _crypto_ accelerationists have been working on for the last 15 years.

The cause of decentralized AI even has a crypto-esque meme to rally around: a mash-up of the gun-rights motto “Come and take it” and the “Don’t tread on me” snake, now snaking out of a GPU on a revolutionary flag.

Yes, it’s a little tinfoil-hat and backwoods-militia. The FBI is probably _not_ going to seize the GPU out of your PlayStation or Xbox. 

But the feds did once make Americans surrender all their gold to the government, so who knows?

Less conspiratorially, the government might regulate model development in a way that would make AI the exclusive domain of a handful of giant corporations.

In the US, at least. Abroad, AI development would likely continue apace…and maybe underground, too, if it can be sufficiently decentralized.

Some of this is already happening. Blockchain-based marketplaces like [Akash](https://akash.network) offer permissionless access to compute, for example. Subnets on the [Bittensor](https://www.bittensor.com) blockchain have been serving and fine-tuning AI models for a couple of years now.

But the holy grail of decentralized AI is training _frontier_ models — models that match the capabilities of Anthropic and OpenAI without
